item.title: LeBron James sends clear message to 76ers after narrow escape against Bucks
item.description: Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images LeBron James has warned the Philadelphia 76ers that they need to improve despite extending their impressive start to the season with a narrow 132-129 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. The 76ers were pushed all the way by a struggling Milwaukee side, with Tyler Herro pouring in 50 points in a performance that nearly produced a major upset. James finished with 21 points, six rebounds, six assists and three steals as Philadelphia improved to 14-3 and maintained its position at the top of the Eastern Conference. LeBron James urges Philadelphia 76ers to improve after Milwaukee Bucks win Speaking to reporters after the game, James admitted there were several areas where the 76ers could have performed better. The veteran forward explained that the players had discussed their mistakes throughout the contest before delivering a clear message about their ambitions. “We had conversations on the bench throughout the game, there’s a lot of things we could have done a lot better,” James said, via Ky Carlin of Sixers Wire. “But this is professional sports, it’s hard to win in professional sports no matter what league it is. So we don’t take that for granted. You know, we accept that for sure with grace. But understanding what we want to be and what we want to accomplish throughout the course of the season. We got to be a lot better.” James’ comments come despite Philadelphia continuing to enjoy one of the strongest starts in the NBA. The 76ers are now tied with the Los Angeles Lakers for the league’s best record at 14-3. Joel Embiid was another major contributor against Milwaukee, finishing with 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists. Tyrese Maxey added 17 points, while Anfernee Simons contributed 18 off the bench. However, the Bucks exposed some weaknesses despite sitting at 1-16 and holding the league’s worst record. Philadelphia will have an opportunity to respond when it hosts the Portland Trail Blazers in its next game. James and his teammates will be keen to deliver a more convincing performance after being pushed so close by Milwaukee. item.title: George Russell: “I don’t regret it” after crashing out of second at Las Vegas GP
item.description: Motorsport photo George Russell could have played it safe and walked away from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix with a podium. Instead, the Mercedes driver gambled on a late lunge for second - and watched both his shot at victory and his championship cushion slide into the Turn 5 barrier. Running third on Lap 48 of 50 behind leader Max Verstappen and team-mate Kimi Antonelli, Russell locked his brakes while trying to clear Antonelli heading into Turn 5. His W17 slid nose-first into the wall, forcing him to reverse back onto the circuit and dropping him to ninth at the chequered flag - 13.192 seconds adrift of Verstappen. Even so, Russell refused to second-guess going for the win. "I knew if I wanted to win the race I needed to be in second going into the last couple of laps," Russell said. "Kimi didn’t have the overtake mode, and I just went for a high-risk move and paid the price, but I don’t regret it. Of course I’m disappointed with it, but I could have been conservative, and I would have finished in third." The miscue drew instant mockery from Verstappen - just a day after their heated FP3 clash - with the Red Bull driver laughing, "Haha, well done. My God," over team radio. Moments later, Antonelli suffered a late power deployment drop that allowed McLaren ’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri past for second and third, leaving Verstappen clear to claim his third Las Vegas win. Salvaging just two points dealt a heavy blow to Russell’s fight for runner-up honours. Verstappen jumped to 304 points - 40 clear of Russell (264) with only 50 points remaining across standard race weekends in Qatar and Abu Dhabi - while Ferrari ’s Lewis Hamilton (267) moved into third and Norris pulled level with Russell on 264. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes “Learning on the fly” in a wild slipstream battle Russell’s late gamble capped a frantic 50-lap tactical puzzle shaped by Formula 1’s 2026 energy-deployment rules, which triggered relentless lead swaps between Verstappen, Russell, Antonelli, and Norris. "It was interesting. It was quite fun for maybe half the race. Then it started to get a bit tiring at one point because it was absolutely impossible to get away," Russell said. "I felt I was in a very good deployment mode to overtake Verstappen and be ahead of the startline. Kimi was overtaking, but Max was already re-overtaking before the line," he added. "But it left me very vulnerable in the middle sector, and that’s why I lost some positions. I went down to P5, and then I had to change my strat mode, and it helped me get back up the order. I felt into the last lap I could go back to what I had to try and win the race. It was tough." Asked how drivers balance straight-line bursts against mid-lap exposure, Russell admitted there was no playbook. "It was just learning on the fly, really," he said. "It was very bizarre. The speed differences in the straight were monumental. I was gaining 1.3s on the straight on Max; it was wild. Strange race." To read

item.title: Brutal Lane Kiffin stat will have fans questioning his LSU hiring
item.description: Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images Brutal Lane Kiffin stat will have fans questioning his LSU hiring appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Throughout the last offseason, LSU football ’s new head coach Lane Kiffin made headlines following his controversial decision to leave Ole Miss and take over at LSU. However, Kiffin’s first season with the Tigers has turned into a hugely disappointing campaign, one he would undoubtedly want to put behind him. LSU’s latest loss to Tennessee has now added another unwanted statistic to Kiffin’s coaching resume. Kiffin has now fallen to 6-20 against AP Top-10 opponents during his head coaching career. Even more concerning, the LSU Tigers have failed to win any of their four matchups against top-10 teams this season, dropping to 0-4 in those games. Overall, Kiffin holds a 15-29 record against ranked opponents. Facing his former team, Kiffin had already received an unwelcome reception from fans, who made their feelings known by flying a banner over Neyland Stadium . The outcome of the game only added to his frustration, as LSU suffered its third consecutive defeat. More disappointingly, all three losses came in games where the Tigers entered as favorites. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Former LSU national champion Breiden Fehoko also didn’t hold back in criticizing Kiffin through an X post following the defeat. “LSU won’t win until Lane Kiffin, Will Wade, & Kim Mulkey start living right,” Fehoko wrote. “Call it what you want, but everything is relative, and the world is all about energy. These 3 head coaches move like snakes in the grass and get applauded on a pedestal. They don’t follow rules; they are scum human beings, and until they right their wrongs, LSU won’t be worth a shit. I promise you everything matters.” Meanwhile, LSU’s disappointing record has become even more difficult to justify considering the resources invested in Kiffin’s first season. Despite having a roster valued at more than $50 million and assembling the nation’s best transfer portal class, the Tigers have managed just a 6-5 record in his debut season. Kiffin will have plenty of questions to address heading into the 2027 season. With expectations significantly higher than the results he has delivered so far, the LSU head coach will need to find solutions quickly. Otherwise, the pressure on his position could intensify considerably. item.title: 'They score when they smile!' - Scott McTominay downs Torino again as Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri drops hilarious touchline quip before Man City reunion
item.description: SSC Napoli v Torino FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Scott McTominay continued his remarkable scoring streak against Torino with a clinical winner that earned injury-hit Napoli a 1-0 Serie A victory. After Massimiliano Allegri joked that his players score when they smile, the former Manchester United midfielder quickly turned his attention to Tuesday's Champions League trip to Manchester City. McTominay strikes again to sink Torino Scott McTominay drilled home a decisive second-half winner from the edge of the box to hand injury-ravaged Napoli a hard-fought 1-0 Serie A victory over Torino. Set up by Noa Lang after the Dutchman sprinted back to halt a Zakaria Aboukhlal counter-attack, the Scotland international buried his shot into the far bottom corner to extend his prolific record against Torino to four goals in just three meetings. The breakthrough sparked a lighthearted reaction from Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri, who turned to his bench and remarked: "See, they score when they smile, I told them to smile more." Speaking afterwards, McTominay echoed that upbeat mood while stressing the need to build consistency. Match-winner calls for momentum after vital victory Despite facing a stubborn Torino side who struck the crossbar through Rolando Mandragora before half-time and forced Lucas Perri into a string of saves from Matteo Politano and Rasmus Hojlund, Napoli held firm for three crucial points. "I am feeling much better," smiled McTominay when speaking to Sky Sport Italia . "It's an important goal, but more importantly we won, we had to win. I'm happy for the fans, we need to get a bit of momentum going, keep winning. In football it's about the next game, and the next game, you have to do your best. We have a team that wants to work, wants to push, and we want to win more games." Injury crisis forces early De Bruyne introduction Allegri reshuffled his depleted squad into a 3-5-2 formation amid an extensive absentee list featuring Alex Meret, Benoit Badiashile, Alisson Santos, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo and Alessandro Buongiorno. Plans to rest 35-year-old Kevin De Bruyne ahead of European duty lasted only 11 minutes, however, as Antonio Vergara limped off in tears with a muscular injury. De Bruyne immediately made his presence felt, slipping a pass through for Hojlund and later teeing up McTominay to test Perri, though his unexpected 79-minute outing added extra fatigue to veteran legs ahead of midweek action. Derby feel awaits McTominay at the Etihad Victory sends Napoli into Tuesday's Champions League clash away at Manchester City in higher spirits, even with Vergara expected to miss the trip. For former Manchester United midfielder McTominay, returning to Manchester carries added personal edge. "A great game, we'll recover now and then think about it from tomorrow," McTominay concluded.

item.title: Collin Graf’s unbelievable Ryan Warsofsky admission amid Sharks’ struggles
item.description: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-Imagn Images Collin Graf’s unbelievable Ryan Warsofsky admission amid Sharks’ struggles appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Jose Sharks entered the 2026-27 season with high hopes for the year ahead. Right now, the once immaculate vibes in San Jose have been run into the ground . Fans are calling for Ryan Warsofsky’s job, and a recent admission from Collin Graf certainly won’t help matters. Graf spoke to reporters following a conversation with Warsofsky. The Sharks have struggled offensively, with Graf being one of the underperformers on this team. However, he was told not to think about offense. In fact, he was seemingly told that goals simply do not matter to his head coach. “Skate faster, play harder. (Warsofsky) also said that he doesn’t care if I score another goal this year,” the Sharks forward said, via beat reporter Curtis Pashelka. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Last season, the Sharks had a very top-heavy offense, with Macklin Celebrini leading the way in historic fashion. This year, San Jose seemingly added offensive reinforcements to help Celebrini out a bit. However, they have struggled mightily to put up goals. The Sharks have the sixth-worst Goals For Per Game in the NHL, according to ESPN. Only the Chicago Blackhawks and Calgary Flames average fewer goals per game than San Jose in the Western Conference. Still, Warsofsky is sticking to a very rigid defensive system. To this point, it has not worked out. The Sharks are 10-12-2, good for fifth in the Pacific Division. However, they have lost nine of their last 14 games. Something has to change before this all snowballs out of control. For San Jose’s sake, hopefully they can make that change sooner rather than later. The Sharks will look for a much-needed win on Monday against the Minnesota Wild.

item.title: Wales boss Wilkinson rules out Fishlock return
item.description: Jess Fishlock scored 48 international goals in 166 games for Wales [FAW] Rhian Wilkinson says she has not considered asking Jess Fishlock to come out of retirement even though the Wales legend will be on camp for the Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway. Fishlock ended her playing career earlier this month after her Seattle Reign side lost to Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-offs. The 39-year-old played on for one final season at Reign having retired from international football in October 2025. Fishlock will be part of Wales' coaching staff for for next month's two-legged tie against the Norwegians, who visit the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later. Despite some speculation over whether Fishlock could play some part on the pitch, Wilkinson said: "I think you get retirement right when you know there's still something in you to give." The Wales boss added: "It takes years to recognise that you got it right, because you're sort of [thinking] 'oh should I have kept playing', but when you get it wrong injuries and someone else makes the decision that you're finished, that's a tough way to to end your career. "I think Jess has qualified [for Euro 2025], made history with Wales, done such a great job as well as building the game over in the US and equally so much in Wales. "[But] she's retired. Jess is here to further her technical and tactical awareness, but also for her experiences and that kind of confidence that she brings to the environment." While there will be no Fishlock, Wales will welcome back a number of experienced players from injury for the Norway games. Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway will likely not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer. The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway. Wales start Nations League with home double-header Wales in fight to retain rising female stars

item.title: Oregon football gets game time for pivotal Washington matchup
item.description: The Ducks and Huskies finally got a game time for their regular-season finale. Oregon will host Washington at 4:30 p.m. Nov. 28 at Autzen Stadium, the Big Ten Conference announced late Saturday. The game will be televised on NBC. A win for Oregon would put the Ducks in the Big Ten Championship game Dec. 5 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The Ducks (8-3, 6-2 Big Ten), who are No. 13 in the College Football Playoff rankings, have won two straight against the Huskies (7-4, 4-4 ) , including last season's 26-14 victory at Husky Stadium in Seattle. Oregon is coming off a 45-7 win against Michigan State Friday night in East Lansing. It was the Ducks' fourth straight victory, the last two of which have come by a combined score of 76-14. Washington upset No. 8 Indiana, 27-24 in overtime Saturday at Husky Stadium. "Counting on our fans to be really annoying and ornery when we get into that stadium, and making that atmosphere so special like it always is at Autzen," coach Dan Lanning said Friday after the win against the Spartans. Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men’s basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com. Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard Newsletter. This article originally appeared on Register-Guard: Oregon football gets game time for pivotal Washington matchup

Oregon is coming off a 45-7 win against Michigan State Friday night in East Lansing. It was the Ducks' fourth straight victory, the last two of which have come by a combined score of 76-14. Washington upset No. 8 Indiana, 27-24 in overtime Saturday at Husky Stadium. "Counting on our fans to be really annoying and ornery when we get into that stadium, and making that atmosphere so special like it always is at Autzen," coach Dan Lanning said Friday after the win against the Spartans. Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men’s basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com. item.title: Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat
item.description: Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia. The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff on Saturday, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations. Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot. Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions. However, they fell agonisingly short. "The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy. "We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard." The 46-year-old former Ospreys coach added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win. "I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again." Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks. "Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said. "So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well." Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales Nations Championship - Australia triumph over Wales - reaction Highs and lows of sport - Lake Dewi Lake has scored three tries in the past two internationals [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup. "It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake. "Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best. "We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times." Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad. "We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain. "We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today. "We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week." Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south. It will be a fifth time Wales and Japan have met in 16 months with Tandy's side defeating Eddie Jones' team 28-21 in Cardiff just two weeks ago. Wales have an injury doubt over scrum-half Tomos Williams who has a tight groin, with Tandy expected

Australia grateful for breaking losing sequence Australia head coach Les Kiss was happy to have broken a four-match losing sequence which included recent defeats against Scotland and England. "I am not only proud but also happy for these boys," said Kiss. "The work they've been putting in over the last four weeks has been good and they just haven't been getting a reward. "Rugby is such a results-driven game and we hadn't been getting the results even though I felt like we weren't far off last week. "To beat a team who just had defeated the All Blacks, in front of 65,000 Wales supporters where the atmosphere was crazy, was special." The Wallabies will now face Ireland on Friday in the contest for fifth place in Twickenham (20:10 GMT) after both sides finished third in their respective pools.

item.title: Chris Finch reveals which Timberwolves player fans can ‘almost set your watch by’
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images Chris Finch reveals which Timberwolves player fans can ‘almost set your watch by’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . MINNEAPOLIS — In a 104-95 victory over the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday, Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jaden McDaniels continued to dominate, leading all scorers with an efficient 25 points, shooting 11-for-17 and attempting just two free throws. In the wake of the injury to star Anthony Edwards, which is expected to sideline the Atlanta native for over two months, it was anticipated that McDaniels would see an increased role in the team’s offense, though at the time McDaniels insisted he didn’t want to change anything about the way he played. Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch commended the “consistency” that McDaniels carries himself with both on and off the court. “Everything about him is consistent,” said Finch. “He’s a consistent person every day. He’s the same guy every day. He has the same routine every day. … You can almost set your watch by everything he does. And so if you’re a consistent person, you have a chance to be a consistent player. He knows who he is as a player, and he plays to that.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaden McDaniels with high praise for LaMelo’s defense this season #RealLoud pic.twitter.com/mfnCRJGYxD — SneakerReporter (@SneakerReporter) November 22, 2026 McDaniels agreed with Finch’s assessment, adding that part of his consistency includes a lack of tardiness. “Yeah, and then I just don’t like being late to anything,” said McDaniels. “Like, it don’t even have to be a deal with the NBA. Like if I got an appointment or something, I just don’t like to be late, for real.” At this point, McDaniels is averaging career-best marks in points per game , rebounds per game, and field goal percentage. With Edwards out and McDaniels’ remarkable efficiency , Finch wants to get him more shot volume. “We made it a point the other night… he’s got to get more shots,” said Finch, who has his team at 9-4 without their best player. “Sometimes we can direct the ball to him, but just the ball’s got to find him. We got to get the ball out of the point of attack quicker and better.” MORE MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES NEWS Chris Finch pinpoints what’s built Timberwolves’ No. 1 defense Is Ty Jerome playing tonight? item.title: BBC Sport comments from ‘neutrals’ on Newcastle United after 2-2 draw against Arsenal
item.description: St. James' Park under the floodlights ahead of kickoff between Newcastle United and Arsenal in November 2026. Interesting to read through these BBC Sport ‘neutrals’ comments, following on from Newcastle United drawing 2-2 with Arsenal. The proverbial game of two halves. Newcastle United not getting a kick in the first half. In the second, United by far the better team. Matthias Jaissle’s triple half-time substitution massively contributing to that. Always interesting to hear the neutral perspectives, as well as from Arsenal fans and the odd Newcastle United supporter… The BBC Sport readers comments from neutrals: ‘Huge respect for how newcastle played from an Arsenal fan here, good luck to you to for the rest of the season.’ ‘Never heard a commentary team so disappointed when Newcastle scored. So biased sky.’ ‘ Even worse with Ian Wright making it into Arsenal TV. Awful coverage.’ ‘Apart from Ian Wright constantly referring to Arsenal as “we”. No, not biased at all.’ ‘As an Arsenal fan, gotta give huge respect to Newcastle, St James Park is always magic. Hate it when Arsenal go 1-0 up and relax, this arrogance is what gets us punished. Take the point, move on.’ ‘Newcastle fans booing when David Raya was on the ground with a potential head injury. Class.’ ‘What head injury? It was his shoulder!’ ‘It’s ridiculous. Gabriel constantly holding and pulling and gets away with it.’ ‘Bad looser.’ ‘Who loost? Sorry, who lost?!!’ ‘Declan Rice (just like Gabriel) is allowed to commit as many fouls as he likes, sometimes a clear free kick isn’t even given, like the one on Barnes at the end, and not receive yellow cards. He could’ve and should’ve had three yellows today. Very tired of the ref being the best player for the opposition, but it’s a common theme.’ ‘First half we were very good, second half a bit complacent along with Newcastle out working us and forcing us into multiple mistakes, they were very good. It was good to get an equaliser but this is what happens when you don’t kill off teams when you are on top. Newcastle very good second half and draw was probably a fair result.’ ‘Newcastle second goal and the dreadful var looking for stuff that isn’t even there . Sucks the life out the game honestly .’ ‘That was strange. There were three Arsenal players in the net, yet they are still looking for offside.’ St. James' Park big screen displays VAR Decision Goal No Offside Offence for Joe Willock with Newcastle United leading Arsenal 2-1 in the 64th minute. Photo by The Mag ‘Well played Newcastle in the second half. Overall, 2-2 draw a fair outcome.’ ‘Raya injuring himself falling to the ground trying to get Osula in trouble was the best bit of the game.’ ‘As a Newcastle fan I’ll take that. I thought it would be 4-0 and Bruno on the score sheet.’ ‘Would’ve been great if Bruno scored, would’ve deserved it for the arrogant booing.’ ‘And how exactly can booing be arrogant???? Bizarre comment.’ ‘Great game to watch as a neutral.’ ‘Well done Newcastle stopped t

item.title: George Russell explains late-race crash in Las Vegas F1 victory bid
item.description: Motorsport photo George Russell has admitted to making “a high-risk move” after crashing with three laps remaining in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in an attempt to clinch victory. As ‘yo-yo’ racing returned to F1, polesitter Max Verstappen and Russell frequently traded the lead throughout the race, occasionally challenged by the sister cars of Isack Hadjar in the first half of the race and Kimi Antonelli later on. On lap 48 of 50, Russell had dropped down to third behind Verstappen and Antonelli and dived down the inside of his team-mate’s Silver Arrow, but locked up and hit the wall. Minimal damage meant he was able to finish the race, albeit down in ninth. “I knew if I wanted to win the race I needed to be in second going into the last couple of laps,” the Briton explained. “Kimi didn't have the overtake mode and I just went for a high-risk move and paid the price, but I don't regret it. Of course I'm disappointed with it, but I could have been conservative and I would have finished in third.” Russell took the lead of the race away from Verstappen on at least six occasions without ever being able to hold on to it, due to the way F1’s new power units – and particularly their batteries and energy deployment – work on this high-speed street circuit. “It was interesting,” the Mercedes driver commented. “I think it was quite fun for maybe half the race. Then it started to get a bit tiring at one point because it was absolutely impossible to get away. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes “I felt I was in a very good deployment mode to overtake Verstappen and be ahead of the start line. Kimi was overtaking but Max was already re-overtaking before the line. But it left me very vulnerable in the middle sector, and that's why I lost some positions. I went down to P5, and then I had to change my strat mode, and it helped me get back up the order. “I felt into the last lap I could go back to what I had to try and win the race. It was tough.” This ‘yo-yo’ type of racing, which is reminiscent of Formula E, hadn’t been seen to this extent since the opening races of the season. “It was just learning on the fly, really,” Russell added. “Yeah, learning on the fly, it was very bizarre. The speed differences in the straight were monumental. I was gaining 1.3s on the straight on Max, it was wild. Strange race.” Russell’s lowly result means he is down to fourth in the drivers’ championship – on equal points with fifth-placed Lando Norris , three points away from Lewis Hamilton and a whopping 40 points adrift of runner-up Verstappen. Read Also: George Russell slams Max Verstappen after Las Vegas clash: ‘He walks around like he’s bigger and better than everyone’ To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
item.description: The Las Vegas Grand Prix featured 'yo-yo racing' throughout the field with regular overtaking [Reuters] Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that saw a non-stop battle for the lead for the entire race. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps, Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap. The world champion dropped to fifth going on to the Strip on the last lap but was able to reclaim the place from Alpine's Pierre Gasly at the end of the long straight. And there was more drama at Ferrari as Charles Leclerc earned a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin. Earlier, Hamilton had been given a 10-second penalty of his own for passing Norris off the track in a fight for position that also involved Leclerc. It was a grand prix more reminiscent of American oval racing than Formula 1, and it depended on unique circumstances revolving around the Las Vegas circuit and energy starved hybrid engines this year. But there was no questioning the showbiz value in the city that prides itself as the entertainment capital of the world. The key stories of an engrossing race were: Verstappen's remarkable intelligence and control in the lead in the most demanding of circumstances Another dip in a dreadful season for Russell More controversy at Ferrari, as both drivers earned 10-second penalties for driving infringements in battles involving the other Verstappen in control despite lead changes Challengers came and went but Max Verstappen was never without the lead for long in Las Vegas [Getty Images] "How many overtakes did I do?" Verstappen asked his engineer on the slowing down lap, as he reflected on a race the like of which F1 has not seen since the famous Monza slipstreaming battles of the 1960s and early 1970s. "Yeah, and not many of them on the straight," his new engineer Tom Hart said, summing up how Verstappen had secured the win against the Mercedes challenge. Lap after lap after lap, Verstappen, who started from pole, would lose the lead to Russell on the Strip only to reclaim it at the last corner, usually going around the outside. If that did not work, and Russell passed later in the lap, or led across the line, Verstappen developed a trademark move around the outside of Turn Three to get back in front. The race went on and on like that, punctuated by a mid-grand prix safety car, but through it all Verstappen always seemed in control. As the race wore on, Antonelli came into the picture after starting sixth, and passed Russell with 12 laps to go to become Verstappen's main challenger. Now it was the Italian's turn to swap places with Verstappen, but again the Dutchman had the measure of Mercedes. At one point, Verstappen asked his team to come up with a better deployment strategy for the final lap because he thought Mercedes had "figured it out". They came back to him to say that he had already come up with the best approach. In the end, though, he need not have worried, as his rivals behind him gave him enough of a gap at the start of the final lap to not have to worry too much about defending his lead. Charles Leclerc (right) dropped to 10th as a result of being given a 10-second penalty for colliding with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton [Getty Images] Verstappen laughs at Russell error That critical final phase started with Russell deciding to make a move to become Verstappen's challenger again. Russell went for a move into Turn Five with two laps to go but he locked up his brakes over the bumps heading into the corner - bumps that had earlier taken Red Bull's Isack Hadjar out of the lead battle when his front wing broke over them - and went straight on into the barrier. Russell managed to reverse out of the barrier but a ninth place finish was not what he was expecting. The incident was also unfortunate for him in the context of his calling out Verstappen's driving after qualifying, when he said "somebody has got to stand up to that guy". Verstappen had the last word, both on track and literally. After seeing Russell's embarrassing mistake, Verstappen came on the radio to say: "Hah, hah. Well done. My God." Now Antonelli looked to be the man who would challenge Verstappen for the win. But that was counting without the McLarens. Piastri had already driven an outstanding race to recover from starting 17th because of an engine penalty and Norris had at one point dropped out of the top 10 in the chaotic lead battle in the first part of the grand prix. But they were third and fourth around the penultimate lap and in what looked like a co-ordinated attack but certainly wasn't, both swept around Antonelli around the outside of the fast final corner heading into the last lap. That gave Verstappen breathing space, and Antonelli was delayed sufficiently that he could not recover to challenge them. Second-placed Norris summed it up, saying: "I think that must have been the most chaotic race ever in the history of Formula 1. I didn't know what was happening half the time." Andrew Benson Q&A: Send us your questions Top 10 1. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 3. Lando Norris (McLaren) 3. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 4. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 5. Pierre Gasly (Alpine) 6. Franco Colapinto (Alpine) 7. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 8. Carlos Sainz (Williams) 9. George Russell (Mercedes) 10. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) Drivers' championship standings Constructors' championship standings What's next? A hectic end to the season means Formula 1 moves from Las Vegas to the Middle East next weekend, for the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit, from 27-29 November. item.title: Jordan Love names two ‘stand-out’ Rams stars who could cause problems for Packers
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Jordan Love has identified Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald as two players who could cause serious problems for the Green Bay Packers when they face the Los Angeles Rams. The Rams have won four consecutive games and arrive at the contest fresh from a convincing 34-6 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Their defensive front is a major reason why Love believes Green Bay face a difficult challenge. However, the Packers could also receive a significant boost of their own, with Micah Parsons making progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury. Jordan Love highlights Los Angeles Rams defensive threat while Micah Parsons makes progress Asked what stands out about the Rams’ defensive front, Love immediately pointed towards Garrett and Donald. “The front, that’s what stands out to you. Obviously, Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, they got a lot of good guys up front. Especially when they’re in base, you get five one-on-one blocks. So yeah, they got some good players over there, so that definitely stands out.” Love also stressed that Green Bay must give him enough protection while creating opportunities in the running game. “Obviously, Myles has been out for a little while, but it’s something that we talk about all week. It starts up front. We gotta handle business. We gotta be able to block the front, give me some time in the run game. We gotta be able to get hands on people, create some lanes in the run game.” Meanwhile, there is encouraging news surrounding Parsons, who returned to practice after tearing his ACL and undergoing meniscus surgery in December 2025. Love was impressed by what he saw from the pass rusher, telling reporters: “You felt his presence out there and that’s what he brings to the table on a daily basis. He’s moving around really well.” Parsons has yet to play this season and Green Bay must decide whether to activate him from the physically unable to perform list. His 21-day practice window is due to close on the day of the Rams game, but his return is not guaranteed. The Packers are taking a cautious approach, with head coach Matt LaFleur making practice performances the key factor in the decision. With the Rams’ defensive front posing a major threat, having Parsons back would be a welcome boost for Green Bay. However, Love and the Packers must prepare for the possibility of facing Los Angeles without him. item.title: Jiri Prochazka Issues Statement After UFC Qatar Loss
item.description: Jiri Prochazka UFC Qatar Getty Former UFC light heavyweight champion Jiri Prochazka issued a statement following his second-round knockout loss at UFC Qatar. Prochazka suffered his second knockout loss of 2027 when he was stopped with two seconds left in the second round by Navajo Stirling in the main event of UFC Qatar on Saturday. It was another tough loss for the Czech native, who dropped to 6-4 in the UFC following the loss, with all four of those defeats coming by knockout. Jiri Prochazka Speaks Out Following UFC Qatar Loss Speaking in a video posted to his social media after losing to Stirling at UFC Qatar, Prochazka shared his reaction to the defeat. “Ah man, I felt sharp, prepared, strong. Maybe too much tactic and not too much pressure. There is a lot of work, it can be much better. No more like this. I will do everything. Believe me,” Prochazka said. An emotional Jiri Prochazka speaks following his loss to Navajo Stirling: "Ah man, I felt sharp, prepared, strong. Maybe too much tactic and not too much pressure. There is a lot of work, it can be much better. No more like this. I will do everything. Believe me." (via… pic.twitter.com/92U3oIr7AO — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 22, 2026 What’s Next for Jiri Prochazka? Following this brutal KO loss against Stirling, it will be interesting to see what move Prochazka makes now to save his UFC career. He is one of the most exciting fighters in the UFC, win or lose, so he’s not at risk of being cut or anything, but if he wants to get back to the belt, then he needs to make a drastic change, and that could mean switching weight classes. Prochazka had previously spoken about moving down to 185 lbs, so it will be interesting to see if a move to the middleweight division could still be in store for him. He is a big man, though, so cutting 20 lbs more off his 205 lbs frame might be really difficult for him to do. Another option is moving up to heavyweight, something that hasn’t been discussed as much as Prochazka moving down in weight. There have been a lot of former light-heavyweight fighters recently who have gone up to heavyweight and found success, namely Johnny Walker, so perhaps this is something that Prochazka could consider, too. Either way, it’s clear that something will have to change after Prochazka has been brutally knocked out by opponents in two straight fights. item.title: Boca Juniors win first international title in 18 years
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Argentina fans celebrate their team's victory at the Obelisk in Buenos Aires after the 2026 FIFA World Cup semi-final soccer match between England and Argentina. (is associated with: «Boca Juniors win first international title in 18 years») Cristina Sille/dpa Argentinian football giants Boca Juniors ended an 18-year wait for an international trophy with a 2-0 victory over Brazil's Atlético Mineiro in the Copa Sudamericana final in Colombia. Santiago Ascacíbar opened the scoring in the 16th minute before Miguel Merentiel doubled the lead shortly after half-time. Backed by an estimated 30,000 to 40,000 travelling supporters in Barranquilla, Boca dominated from the start, with Mineiro creating few chances. Thousands of fans also gathered around Buenos Aires' landmark Obelisk and outside the club's La Bombonera stadium to celebrate the triumph. The Copa Sudamericana is South America's equivalent of the UEFA Europa League, sitting below the continent's premier club competition, the Copa Libertadores. Boca last won an international trophy in 2008, when they lifted the Recopa Sudamericana. Celebrations were briefly overshadowed when Boca midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed during a live television interview after the match. The Argentina international received medical attention and was taken to hospital as a precaution. He later posted a photo from the clinic on Instagram, saying it was "just a dizzy spell." Boca coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena said Paredes had already felt dizzy during the match and was substituted in the 58th minute. Temperatures of around 30 degrees Celsius and high humidity had troubled players throughout the game.

item.title: Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints Picks and Predictions
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball against the New Orleans Saints during the second quarter at Soldier Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Windy City Gridiron crew makes their pick and some predictions for the Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints game. Sam Householder: I’m trying to recalibrate my expectations. I think the Bears are due for a blowout. Coming off the bye, heading into a tough stretch, they can’t be caught in a look-ahead spot, and I don’t think Ben will let them. This is the worst defense they’ve faced in a month and probably all season. Bears 38, Saints 14 Josh Sunderbruch: I think there’s rust to shake off, and for about a quarter or two it looks closer than it should, followed by the Bears steadily pulling away. Final score: Bears 31, Saints 17, with backups playing the final drive. Mongo Peanut: The Bears come out of the bye on fire, with their running game tuned up for a playoff push. The Saints hit a couple of shots to Olave, but otherwise look lifeless after a letdown against Carolina. Bears 38, Saints 13. Jacob Infante: The Bears looked sloppier than expected against the Buccaneers, but they still found a way to win. That’s the sign of a good team, and knowing Ben Johnson, he used this bye week to recalibrate and get the offense back on track. I trust Chicago to get out to an early lead and force the Saints to play from behind, where I can see Jeffery Simmons tallying two sacks for the afternoon. Bears 34, Saints 20 Gary Baugher Jr.: I have the Bears by at least two touchdowns this week; the ground game is going to get back on track, Caleb Williams will throw for 2+ TDs, and Tyler Shough will be sacked 4+ times. Shough to Olave deep has worked all season, so I expect them linking up a few times, but a lack of a ground game and identity on the OL and the defense as a whole for the Saints will make this a lopsided affair. Bears 38, Saints 17 (edited) Jeff Berckes: My colleagues are predicting offensive point totals in the 30s, and I say… why so conservative?! My colleagues are also allowing for the Saints to get into the end zone. Why so scared? Ben got a chance to get in the lab. Dennis Allen Revenge Game. I’ll say Bears 70, Saints negative 3. TJ Starman: I think there’s plenty of reason to expect fireworks on this game. While the Bears are firmly the better team, I wouldn’t be surprised to see the Saints trade a few haymakers along the way (or even in garbage time) in a matchup more akin to Carolina/Atlanta than Tampa Bay. Bears win big, 41 – 24 Lester A. Wiltfong Jr.: I predicted Bears 38, Saints 17 earlier this week, so I’ll stick with that. Even though Kyle Monangai is back, I think D’Andre Swift will have a big day, with 100+ yards on the ground and another touchdown. Caleb will get his too, with 3 passing TDs and over 300 total yards. Superfans: Not gonna lie… we came here to drop another ston

item.title: Super Formula Suzuka: Tomoki Nojiri breaks drought with win in season finale
item.description: Motorsport photo Tomoki Nojiri ended a year-long Super Formula win drought in the final race of the season at Suzuka on Sunday, beating newly-crowned champion Kakunoshin Ohta . Team Mugen driver Nojiri converted a record-extending 26th pole into a first victory since the penultimate round of the season last year by a margin of 2.5 seconds, holding off a charge from Dandelion Racing's Ohta in the closing laps. After a relatively uneventful opening stint in which he led fellow front-row starter Nirei Fukuzumi , Nojiri completed his mandatory stop on lap 12 of 31, but encountered slower traffic as Ohta embarked on an ambitious overcut strategy. With no safety car, Ohta showed strong pace on older rubber before his stop on lap 26, but afterwards he not only slipped behind Nojiri but also the yet-to-stop Giuliano Alesi. Once clear of Alesi, Ohta rapidly cut down the eight-second advantage that Nojiri had, setting a succession of fastest laps, but was unable to catch the two-time champion. Saturday race winner and series runner-up Ayumu Iwasa completed the podium in third, but lacked the pace of team-mate Nojiri and was a distant 20.6 seconds adrift at the finish. The Red Bull Formula 1 reserve had to fend off a strong late challenge from Rookie Racing driver Fukuzumi, who slipped behind Iwasa on cold tyres as he struggled on his out lap. Ayumu Iwasa, TEAM MUGEN AUTOBACS Ayumu Iwasa, TEAM MUGEN AUTOBACS Fukuzumi was best of the Toyota drivers in fourth behind an all-Honda top three, ahead of Tadasuke Makino (Dandelion) and Kamui Kobayashi (TGM Grand Prix). Williams F1 reserve Luke Browning secured Rookie of the Year in seventh place for Kondo Racing, his best finish since May's Suzuka round. Browning made it through to Q2 for the first time of the year in dry conditions, albeit starting 12th after having his best lap deleted for track limits, but jumped to seventh on the first lap. Like Ohta, Browning elected to leave his pit stop late, until lap 29, but after slipping behind Kobayashi on his out lap he was unable to make up places on new tyres. Completing the points scorers were Cerumo/Inging drivers Sena Sakaguchi and Toshiki Oyu , who swapped places on the last lap as Sakaguchi swept around the outside at 130R, and Nakajima Racing’s Ren Sato . Nakajima Racing missed out on overhauling TOM’S for third in the teams’ standings, not helped by Fraga starting last after a mysterious electrical shutdown in qualifying. Fraga could only recover to 14th in the race, but kept hold of third in the drivers’ standings. TOM’S endured a disastrous final race of the season as Formula 2-bound Sho Tsuboi damaged his front wing after contact with Yuto Nomura’s B-Max Racing car, forcing him into an early stop for a new nose on his way to 19th place. Sacha Fenestraz meanwhile was a lowly 20th after spinning on cold tyres on his out lap and clipping Nomura, damaging his nose in the process. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman toasts seniors after beating SMU
item.description: Michael Clubb/South Bend Tribune / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman toasts seniors after beating SMU appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Marcus Freeman was proud of his seniors for defending home field in their regular-season home finale in the No. 6 Notre Dame Fighting Irish’s 24-3 win over the SMU Mustangs on Saturday night. Freeman has been the Fighting Irish’s head coach since 2021, going through his sixth season with the program. He shines as one of the best coaches in the country, having led Notre Dame to the national championship game in 2024. Going into the clash with SMU, Notre Dame was playing its last home game of the regular season. They are on a mission to reach the College Football Playoffs, missing the cut last year. They got the job done by dominating SMU on both sides of the ball, as Freeman thanked the seniors for playing great after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “At the end of the day, we got them a victory, and that’s what it was all about. No matter how you got it, I just want them to have this feeling on their last guaranteed home game, and I’m proud of everybody that had a part of it,” Freeman said. Marcus Freeman joins Kathryn Tappen fresh off a Senior Night victory! 🍀 pic.twitter.com/uwUkDjv0Jb — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 22, 2026 How Marcus Freeman, Notre Dame performed against SMU Marcus Freeman and Notre Dame are on great pace to make the College Football Playoffs. Beating SMU in convincing fashion at home puts them one step closer to achieving success. Notre Dame did most of its damage in the first half, leading 17-3 at halftime. SMU failed to create any sparks of a rally, being unable to keep up with the Fighting Irish powerhouse. CJ Carr had a decent outing leading the offense. He completed 19 out of 29 passes for 312 yards and one touchdown and an interception. Nolan James Jr. led the run game with 15 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown, while Jordan Faison topped receivers with seven catches for 109 yards and a touchdown. The No. 6 Fighting Irish will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Syracuse Orange in Week 13 as kickoff commences on Nov. 28 at 12 p.m. ET. Marcus Freeman was proud of his seniors for defending home field in their regular-season home finale in the No. 6 Notre Dame Fighting Irish’s 24-3 win over the SMU Mustangs on Saturday night. Freeman has been the Fighting Irish’s head coach since 2021, going through his sixth season with the program. He shines as one of the best coaches in the country, having led Notre Dame to the national championship game in 2024. Going into the clash with SMU, Notre Dame was playing its last home game of the regular season. They are on a mission to reach the College Football Playoffs, missing the cut last year. They got the job done by dominating SMU on both sides of the ball, as Freeman thanked the seniors for playing great after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “At the end of the day, we got them a victory, and that’s what it was all about. No matter how you got it, I just want them to have this feeling on their last guaranteed home game, and I’m proud of everybody that had a part of it,” Freeman said. Marcus Freeman joins Kathryn Tappen fresh off a Senior Night victory! 🍀 pic.twitter.com/uwUkDjv0Jb — NBC Sports (@NBCSports) November 22, 2026 How Marcus Freeman, Notre Dame performed against SMU Marcus Freeman and Notre Dame are on great pace to make the College Football Playoffs. Beating SMU in convincing fashion at home puts them one step closer to achieving success. Notre Dame did most of its damage in the first half, leading 17-3 at halftime. SMU failed to create any sparks of a rally, being unable to keep up with the Fighting Irish powerhouse. CJ Carr had a decent outing leading the offense. He completed 19 out of 29 passes for 312 yards and one touchdown and an interception. Nolan James Jr. led the run game with 15 carries for 98 yards and a touchdown, while Jordan Faison topped receivers with seven catches for 109 yards and a touchdown. The No. 6 Fighting Irish will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Syracuse Orange in Week 13 as kickoff commences on Nov. 28 at 12 p.m. ET. item.title: 3 Takeaways as Wembanyama's 50-point night leads Spurs past Pelicans
item.description: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks against the New Orleans Pelicans during the second quarter of the NBA game at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Wembanyama scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds in 32 minutes as the Spurs defeated the Pelicans 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whatever Spurs coach Mitch Johnson had drawn up for Saturday's game against New Orleans, it didn't take long for Victor Wembanyama to render it obsolete. The new game plan was considerably simpler. "Just get him the ball," forward Keldon Johnson said. The Spurs did. Wembanyama delivered. In a statistical line that has never been recorded in NBA history, Wembanyama finished with 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals to lead a dominating 114-91 victory over the Pelicans. It marked Wembanyama's second 50-point game of the season, joining a 52-point, 24-rebound effort in a Nov. 4 win over Dallas. He came within one board of making it his second 50-20 game as well. Wembanyama put up 17 points in the first quarter, a career high for a single frame. No player in the NBA this season had posted a game with at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His 32 points in the first half Saturday would have been a Spurs franchise record, were it not for the 37 he put on the L.A. Lakers last season. The 22-year-old All-Star views his personal accolades as a byproduct of team success. "It just comes when we play the right way," said Wembanyama, who finished 20 of 29 from the field and 5 of 11 from 3-point distance. "I just want to stack them up, many more." Stephon Castle added 19 points and five 3-pointers for the Spurs, who improved to 9-0 this season against teams with losing records. Jeremiah Fears scored 29 points and Jordan Poole had 25 for the Pelicans, who were playing without star forward Zion Williamson (thigh contusion). New Orleans had little answer for Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4 Frenchman who transformed the Frost Bank Center into his personal playground. With Wembanyama chasing his third career 50-point game, coach Mitch Johnson allowed him to remain on the floor into the fourth quarter of an increasingly lopsided affair. San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) and forward Harrison Barnes (40) play in the fourth quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Wembanyama reached the half-century mark on a step-back 3-pointer with 6:30 remaining, then exited to a standing ovation. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Mitch Johnson said. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50." Asked if he would have had to spar with Wembanyama if he had tried to lift him with 47 points, the coach laughed. "No comment," he said. Here are three takeaways from Saturday's game, which improved the Spurs' record to 14-3,

Wembanyama scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds in 32 minutes as the Spurs defeated the Pelicans 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Whatever Spurs coach Mitch Johnson had drawn up for Saturday's game against New Orleans, it didn't take long for Victor Wembanyama to render it obsolete. The new game plan was considerably simpler. "Just get him the ball," forward Keldon Johnson said. The Spurs did. Wembanyama delivered. In a statistical line that has never been recorded in NBA history, Wembanyama finished with 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals to lead a dominating 114-91 victory over the Pelicans. It marked Wembanyama's second 50-point game of the season, joining a 52-point, 24-rebound effort in a Nov. 4 win over Dallas. He came within one board of making it his second 50-20 game as well. Wembanyama put up 17 points in the first quarter, a career high for a single frame. No player in the NBA this season had posted a game with at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals. Wembanyama had that by halftime. His 32 points in the first half Saturday would have been a Spurs franchise record, were it not for the 37 he put on the L.A. Lakers last season. The 22-year-old All-Star views his personal accolades as a byproduct of team success. "It just comes when we play the right way," said Wembanyama, who finished 20 of 29 from the field and 5 of 11 from 3-point distance. "I just want to stack them up, many more." Stephon Castle added 19 points and five 3-pointers for the Spurs, who improved to 9-0 this season against teams with losing records. Jeremiah Fears scored 29 points and Jordan Poole had 25 for the Pelicans, who were playing without star forward Zion Williamson (thigh contusion). New Orleans had little answer for Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4 Frenchman who transformed the Frost Bank Center into his personal playground. With Wembanyama chasing his third career 50-point game, coach Mitch Johnson allowed him to remain on the floor into the fourth quarter of an increasingly lopsided affair. San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) and forward Harrison Barnes (40) play in the fourth quarter of an NBA game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. The Spurs won 114-91. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Wembanyama reached the half-century mark on a step-back 3-pointer with 6:30 remaining, then exited to a standing ovation. "I was just hoping he got to 50 when he did," Mitch Johnson said. "It would have been hard to take him out that close to 50." Asked if he would have had to spar with Wembanyama if he had tried to lift him with 47 points, the coach laughed. "No comment," he said. Here are three takeaways from Saturday's game, which improved the Spurs' record to 14-3, tied with Philadelphia and the Lakers for tops in the NBA: 1. Another crazy on/off night for Wemby For what is becoming a nightly occurrence, Victor Wembanyama's on/off numbers were eye-popping Saturday. The Spurs were a plus-35 with Wembanyama on the floor. They were a minus-12 when he sat. For those doing the math, that's a 47-point swing. Read that again. The Spurs were 47 points better with Wembanyama on the court than they were with him on the bench. It didn't matter much against the lowly Pelicans, but that kind of drop-off can be costly against better opponents. And it has been. Fans might be tempted to pin the problem on Wembanyama's backup, Luke Kornet. That analysis, however, feels a bit too simplistic. It's probably true Kornet hasn't been quite the game-saving force he was at this point last season. He was a minus-11 Saturday in a game the Spurs won by 23. Wembanyama said maybe going for 50 wasn't ethical basketball but the other greats like Wilt didn't stop at 98 points. It is a balance and about playing the right way when it counts https://t.co/C62OAq8Wyr - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) November 22, 2026 Still, plus-minus can be a misleading measure of Kornet's value. Wembanyama, naturally, is a tide that lifts the plus-minus numbers of everyone around him. Kornet, by definition, is the only regular rotation player who never shares the floor with Wembanyama and therefore never gets the benefit of the Wemby boost. Coach Mitch Johnson sees the problems during the non-Wemby minutes as more of a collective failure than a Kornet problem. "The worst minutes of the non-Victor minutes has nothing to do with Luke, in my opinion," Johnson said. "It's when we take quick shots and then we get in transition defense a lot and we're on our heels. If we could shore that up, it would help our defense and our offense more than anything else." 2. Fox not sweating low scoring night It was another quiet night in the scoring column for De'Aaron Fox, who has perhaps counterintuitively attempted just nine shots combined in the two games since Dylan Harper went down with an injury. With Wembanyama going nuclear against New Orleans, the Spurs hardly needed Fox to join the scoring barrage. Fox finished Saturday 1 of 4 from the field for five points. He also handed out a team-high 10 assists and finished a plus-33. It was a different sort of quiet night than Thursday against the Clippers, when Fox went 2 of 5 for 10 points in 32 minutes of a 124-112 victory. There is no question the Spurs need Fox to remain aggressive with Harper, their second-leading scorer, sidelined. Fox insists he hasn't changed his approach, even if the shots haven't been falling - or coming - at the same rate. "When we have guys out, we have guys that step into a little bit different roles," Fox said. "But the approach is still the same." Does he believe he needs to look for his own shot more with Harper out? "I definitely don't look at it that way," Fox said. 3. Speaking of assists … The Spurs handed out at least 30 assists for the second consecutive game Saturday and the sixth time this season. They are 6-0 in those games. Wembanyama had plenty to do with the latest assist bonanza. Fourteen of the Spurs' assists resulted in baskets by the All-Star center. Fox led the way with 10, while Stephon Castle added six and Keldon Johnson chipped in four. The formula isn't complicated. When the Spurs move the ball like they did against the Pelicans, they are awfully difficult to beat. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Bayern Munich president not worried about Michael Olise transfer rumors
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 20: Michael Olise of FC Bayern Munich during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between FC Bayern München and 1. FC Köln at Allianz Arena on November 20, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images It’s no surprise that Michael Olise is in high demand among top clubs across Europe’s top five leagues, but the Bayern Munich winger has not personally expressed any desire to leave the German Rekordmeister . His contract with Bayern runs through June 2029—he signed a five-year deal when he joined from Crystal Palace in the summer of 2024—and Bayern hopes to have him sign a contract extension, following in the footsteps of Dayot Upamecano and Harry Kane. With his nonchalant, relaxed manner off the pitch, Olise is not a man of many words in front of a microphone, making it hard to tell whether he is thinking about a new challenge away from Munich soon or wants to stay long-term. Right now, Bayern has not yet sat down with the player and/or his representatives for concrete discussions about his future. Even so, the club remains relaxed about his contract situation despite heavy interest from clubs like Real Madrid and Liverpool. Speaking at Bayern’s annual general meeting, club president Herbert Hainer echoed that the front office is not worried about Olise’s contract and is, for now, focused on his football. “As for all the rumors surrounding Michael, we are very relaxed. He has a contract until 2029. And let me also say something about you as a person, dear Michael. I would much rather have someone who makes a statement with the ball at his feet than someone who makes headlines with a microphone in front of him! Because the fans want genuine characters and personalities who stand out. And dear Michael, first and foremost, I wish you a speedy recovery. Don’t let anyone change you . Stay exactly as you are,” Hainer passionately said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Olise himself narrowly avoided a serious injury when a challenge from behind caused his ankle to roll and land awkwardly just before halftime in Bayern’s 1-1 draw with FC Köln on Friday evening. With an injury list that now includes Harry Kane, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Manuel Neuer, and Luis Díaz, Vincent Kompany will be relieved that nothing too serious happened to Olise. Bayern’s attack looked noticeably different without both Kane and Olise — a testament to how much they mean to the team. Time will tell what happens with Olise, though Bayern handled the extensions for Upamecano and Kane with the same calm approach, which bodes well for talks with him. Join the conversation! item.title: UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach gets encouraging update after OT injury vs. Michigan
item.description: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach gets encouraging update after OT injury vs. Michigan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . UCLA football absorbed two costly losses in Ann Arbor Saturday. One became the costly 18-16 loss to Michigan . But the other loss involved quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who left in scary fashion. Dieffenbach suffered a leg injury and needed the medical cart to come out. Coach Bob Chesney eventually leaned into the younger brother of the other injured Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava Madden. So now Bruin fans are on pins and needles wondering if Chesney and company just lost their second QB for good. Except CBS Los Angeles sports reporter Jill Painter Lopez provided an encouraging update there . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “X-Rays were negative on UCLA football QB Ty Dieffenbach, according to a source with knowledge of the situation,” Lopez posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter. So Dieffenbach appears to have no breaks in his bones, allowing UCLA to dodge disaster there. But it also doesn’t mean he’ll be fully healthy for the USC showdown on Nov. 28, which takes place inside the Rose Bowl. Chesney may need to prepare the younger Iamaleava for what will become the biggest game of his career. And one that will seal UCLA’s Big Ten title game and College Football Playoff fate. UCLA’s loss now helps three-loss Oregon greatly. The Ducks have re-emerged into the conference championship race and now, appears to control their own destiny. Oregon also received help from Indiana falling to Washington on Saturday. A Oregon versus UCLA rematch from the Bruins’ 17-15 road win in Eugene could be in the works. But a UCLA loss, then Iowa beating Nebraska, pits the Ducks and Hawkeyes as the Dec. 5 showdown. (Photo by Daniel Bartel/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bulls continue their three-game homestand on Sunday, hosting the Denver Nuggets at the United Center. The Bulls are coming off a 98-94 loss to the Washington Wizards on Friday. They blew a 15-point lead after scoring just nine points in the third quarter. On the other hand, the Nuggets are starting to build momentum and have won two in a row. They have also won seven of their last 10 games. Chicago Bulls Make Roster Decision Before Sunday’s Game In a post on X, formerly known as Twitter, the Chicago Bulls announced that they have recalled Dailyn Swain from the Windy City Bulls in the NBA G League. “Roster Update: We have recalled G/F Dailyn Swain from the @windycitybulls,” the Bulls announced. Roster Update: We have recalled G/F Dailyn Swain from the @windycitybulls . https://t.co/WC8B89kFm4 — Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) November 21, 2026 The Bulls initially assigned the rookie guard to the G League on Thursday. He started in the Windy City’s win over the Noblesville Boom, finishing with 16 points, eight rebounds and nine assists on 6-for-14 shooting. In three games in the G League so far this season, Swain is averaging 19.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.7 steals. He’s shooting just 41.5 percent from the field but is knocking down 40.0 percent of his 3-point shots. Daily Swain This Season Getty Dailyn Swain #5 of the Chicago Bulls dribbles the ball as Cody Williams #9 of the Minnesota Timberwolves falls down during the second half of a preseason game at the United Center on October 16, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. Roster Update: We have recalled G/F Dailyn Swain from the @windycitybulls . https://t.co/WC8B89kFm4 — Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) November 21, 2026 The Bulls initially assigned the rookie guard to the G League on Thursday. He started in the Windy City’s win over the Noblesville Boom, finishing with 16 points, eight rebounds and nine assists on 6-for-14 shooting. In three games in the G League so far this season, Swain is averaging 19.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.0 assists and 1.7 steals. He’s shooting just 41.5 percent from the field but is knocking down 40.0 percent of his 3-point shots. Daily Swain This Season Getty Dailyn Swain #5 of the Chicago Bulls dribbles the ball as Cody Williams #9 of the Minnesota Timberwolves falls down during the second half of a preseason game at the United Center on October 16, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. The Chicago Bulls selected Dailyn Swain with the 15th overall pick of the 2026 NBA draft. Swain was even called a steal back then, but he has since struggled to get into coach Tiago Splitter ‘s rotation. In just four games this season, Swain is averaging 1.8 points and 1.3 rebounds on 22.2 percent shooting. He hasn’t earned the trust of his head coach amid the team’s slow start to the campaign. Swain had a rough summer after the draft. He struggled in the Summer League and followed it up with a subpar preseason. Splitter even told reporters ahead of the G League’s season opener that the rookie guard will spend time with the Windy City Bulls to continue his development. Will Dailyn Swain Play vs. Nuggets? Getty Head coach Tiago Splitter of the Chicago Bulls looks on against the Minnesota Timberwolves during the first half of the preseason game at the United Center on October 16, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. With just four games this season, Dailyn Swain is unlikely to see any minutes against the Denver Nuggets unless there’s a blowout. However, Norman Powell is questionable to play due to a strained right hamstring. If Powell is downgraded to out, it won’t be surprising if Swain’s number gets called up. The Bulls are 3-2 since Caleb Wilson went down with an injury. They have been playing better overall, though they still have a lot of work to do. item.title: ‘Wilt (Chamberlain) Reincarnated,’ ‘Video Game Stat Line’ — Hoops Fans Heap Praise on Victor Wembanyama’s ‘Unreal Performance’ vs. Pelicans
item.description: ‘Wilt (Chamberlain) Reincarnated,’ ‘Video Game Stat Line’ — Hoops Fans Heap Praise on Victor Wembanyama’s ‘Unreal Performance’ vs. Pelicans Victor Wembanyama keeps putting up numbers that are difficult to believe. The San Antonio Spurs star scored 50 points and grabbed 19 rebounds Saturday in a 114-91 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, giving him his second 50-point game in November. The performance quickly drew comparisons to video games and Wilt Chamberlain, while others were already talking about the MVP race. Fans See an MVP Case Taking Shape After Victor Wembanyama’s Latest Dominant Outing SportsCenter summed up the performance with a tweet: “Victor Wembanyama just dropped another video game stat line. 50 and 19. Wemby is unreal.” Hoop Central also highlighted the 7-foot-4 center’s remarkable numbers. He shot 20-for-29 from the field and finished with a plus-35 rating, the best mark in the game. “Unreal performance,” the account posted. The Pelicans briefly took control in the first quarter after falling behind by 11. Jordan Poole hit three 3-pointers in a little more than a minute, helping New Orleans take a 26-23 lead with 3:10 remaining. Wembanyama answered by scoring San Antonio’s final 9 points of the period, including a 3-pointer and a fadeaway jumper that put the Spurs ahead 32-29. San Antonio never trailed again. The two-time All-Star entered halftime with 32 points as the Spurs built a 61-45 lead. He reached 40 by the end of the third quarter before Stephon Castle found him for the 3-pointer that gave him 50 with 6:29 remaining. It was his second 3-pointer in 46 seconds. The 2024 Rookie of the Year also showed his range, finishing 5-for-11 from 3-point range after shooting 30% from deep entering the game. One fan brought up the highly anticipated video game release, writing : “After GTA 6 Wemby is crazy.” The 2026 Western Conference Finals MVP is also building an early case for another major individual honor. He was the unanimous 2025-26 Defensive Player of the Year and helped the Spurs reach the NBA Finals. San Antonio has carried that momentum into this season, opening with a 14-3 record. Another fan was already looking beyond his defensive credentials : “Bro really on track for MVP, DPOY, FMVP and a chip.” Through his first 16 games, Wembanyama averaged 28.6 ppg and 11.9 rpg while shooting 52.8% from the field. He surpassed both averages by halftime against New Orleans. One fan put his performance in historical terms : “In 32 minutes … we’re watching Wilt reincarnated lol. This is the MVP.” Another brought Luka Dončić into the discussion, commenting : “Luka FC thought they were getting MVP.” The Pelicans had little answer for the Spurs star, particularly with several key players unavailable. item.title: NFL Makes Final Decision on Punishment for ‘Dirty’ Travis Kelce Hit
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce hits a huge record before suffering an ankle injury against the Falcons. Getty Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce shared his thoughts on what some fans thought was a “dirty” hit that left him briefly injured against the Atlanta Falcons last week, and the NFL has now had its final say on the play. Kelce was hurt after Atlanta Falcons safety DeMarcco Hellams tackled him low, aggravating an already injured ankle. There was some speculation that Hellams may have intentionally tried to injure Kelce, and the Chiefs tight end would not say one way or the other. But the league decided on Saturday that Hellams did not run afoul of any rules with the hit. NFL Decides Against Fine for Falcons Player The NFL announced fines for all Week 10 games on Saturday, with nothing listed for the Falcons in their loss to the Chiefs last week. Kelce had addressed the hit on his “New Heights” podcast this week, answering a question from a fan who called the hit “dirty.” “I don’t know if that was the case; the way he tackled me… and I just got caught in a bad position,” Kelce replied. “You know, that’s football. And on the flip side, you know, if it was a quote-unquote intentional, you know, extra grab and turn of the ankle, you know, it’s just part of it.” Kelce agreed that the play did not warrant a flag, as Hellams made a legal hit, but said it did leave him hurt. The Chiefs tight end was in visible pain and briefly left the game, but was able to return. “I don’t think it was, you know, crazy enough for it to get a flag or it to be a fine or anything like that,” Kelce said. “Obviously, in the moment, I thought it was, because it hurt like hell.” Chiefs Have Chance to Make Up Ground The Chiefs have turned their attention to Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, where they will face a well-traveled veteran quarterback. The Cardinals ruled out Carson Beck, handing the ball instead to Josh Johnson. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur shared praise for the 40-year-old. “You’ve got to have a baseline talent level, which clearly half the league has felt like [Johnson] has,” LaFleur said. “He is incredible in the quarterback room. He’s incredible for the starter. He’s incredible for young quarterbacks in terms of just the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He’s mature, and he can still sling it. He’s been in this league. It’s not like he was just on the street.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post NFL Makes Final Decision on Punishment for ‘Dirty’ Travis Kelce Hit appeared first on HEAVY .
