item.title: Defense Carries Irish Over SMU
item.description: Notre Dame’s defense made key stops in critical moments as the Irish won by 24-3 on Senior Night. SMU’s potent offense poked holes in Notre Dame throughout the evening but failed to breach the goal line. CJ Carr and the Irish attack sputtered at times and stopped themselves with two careless turnovers. Several explosive plays were the difference in the game as Carr hit long passes to multiple receivers. The win moves Notre Dame to 10-1 on the season on a wild day of upsets in college football. SMU stunned the Irish on the opening series when Kendrick Raphael broke off a 70-yard run to reach the red zone. Notre Dame held but paid a heavy price as Luke Talich suffered a significant injury defending a pass. Kicker Brendan Baird came on to put the Mustangs on the board with a short field goal. A fumbled snap blew up the play and the Irish took over. Carr moved the hosts and found Jordan Faison across midfield. Faison lost the ball while fighting for additional yards and SMU recovered. It seemed then as though it was going to be one of those ugly games. The Mustangs could not capitalize but caught a break when their punt came to rest on the Irish one. Jaden Greathouse caught the first of several deep throws by Carr and rambled 62 yards. A pass interference penalty set up a short scoring run by Cooper Flanagan from a full house backfield. This capped a 99-yard drive and an anxious crowd breathed a sigh of relief. Quarterback Kevin Jennings and the Mustangs responded as the game moved into the second period. The drive ran out of gas in Irish territory as Baird nailed a 40-yard field goal. This cut Notre Dame’s advantage to 7-3. Carr looked to Faison as the Mustang defense began loading up against the run. They connected for 31 yards before Faison made a spectacular one-handed touchdown catch on a corner route. Jordan Faison (6) had a great night against SMU (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire) Trailing by 14-3, Jennings rallied his team by hitting Yamir Knight for 34 yards to reach Irish territory. A few plays later, Jennings went for broke and lofted a long pass to Jalen Cooper near the pylon. Irish cornerback Jaylen Sanders made a leaping interception and fell into the end zone. The teams exchanged punts before Notre Dame took over with 34 seconds remaining in the half. Carr hit Jack Larsen for 25 yards and Micah Gilbert for 37 more as the seconds ticked away. After yet another fade pass fell harmlessly to the turf, the Irish settled for a Spencer Porath field goal. This stretched their lead to 17-3 as the half ended. Notre Dame received the kickoff to open the third quarter and started fast. Nolan James ripped off a 38-yard run into the Mustang red zone. James completed the drive moments later with a four yard touchdown burst. The score stood at 24-3 with over 25 minutes remaining in the game. No one could have guessed these would be the last points of the night. Later in the period, Jennings hit Knight for a long gain to the Irish five yard line
item.content:encoded: Notre Dame’s defense made key stops in critical moments as the Irish won by 24-3 on Senior Night. SMU’s potent offense poked holes in Notre Dame throughout the evening but failed to breach the goal line. CJ Carr and the Irish attack sputtered at times and stopped themselves with two careless turnovers. Several explosive plays were the difference in the game as Carr hit long passes to multiple receivers. The win moves Notre Dame to 10-1 on the season on a wild day of upsets in college football. SMU stunned the Irish on the opening series when Kendrick Raphael broke off a 70-yard run to reach the red zone. Notre Dame held but paid a heavy price as Luke Talich suffered a significant injury defending a pass. Kicker Brendan Baird came on to put the Mustangs on the board with a short field goal. A fumbled snap blew up the play and the Irish took over. Carr moved the hosts and found Jordan Faison across midfield. Faison lost the ball while fighting for additional yards and SMU recovered. It seemed then as though it was going to be one of those ugly games. The Mustangs could not capitalize but caught a break when their punt came to rest on the Irish one. Jaden Greathouse caught the first of several deep throws by Carr and rambled 62 yards. A pass interference penalty set up a short scoring run by Cooper Flanagan from a full house backfield. This capped a 99-yard drive and an anxious crowd breathed a sigh of relief. Quarterback Kevin Jennings and the Mustangs responded as the game moved into the second period. The drive ran out of gas in Irish territory as Baird nailed a 40-yard field goal. This cut Notre Dame’s advantage to 7-3. Carr looked to Faison as the Mustang defense began loading up against the run. They connected for 31 yards before Faison made a spectacular one-handed touchdown catch on a corner route. Jordan Faison (6) had a great night against SMU (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire) Trailing by 14-3, Jennings rallied his team by hitting Yamir Knight for 34 yards to reach Irish territory. A few plays later, Jennings went for broke and lofted a long pass to Jalen Cooper near the pylon. Irish cornerback Jaylen Sanders made a leaping interception and fell into the end zone. The teams exchanged punts before Notre Dame took over with 34 seconds remaining in the half. Carr hit Jack Larsen for 25 yards and Micah Gilbert for 37 more as the seconds ticked away. After yet another fade pass fell harmlessly to the turf, the Irish settled for a Spencer Porath field goal. This stretched their lead to 17-3 as the half ended. Notre Dame received the kickoff to open the third quarter and started fast. Nolan James ripped off a 38-yard run into the Mustang red zone. James completed the drive moments later with a four yard touchdown burst. The score stood at 24-3 with over 25 minutes remaining in the game. No one could have guessed these would be the last points of the night. Later in the period, Jennings hit Knight for a long gain to the Irish five yard line. Remarkably, the defense dug in and forced incompletions on third and fourth downs. It appeared Notre Dame would embark on another long scoring drive after securing a pair of first downs. It was not to be. Carr got greedy as he bypassed an open receiver to take a deep shot into coverage. Jayvon Thomas intercepted it on the first play of the final quarter. The Irish defense frustrated Jennings and the Mustangs once again as Elijah Hughes recorded a 13-yard sack. SMU punted the ball to the Notre Dame three yard line. When the Irish fell short on third down, punter Jasper Scaife blasted a 76-yard bomb. It was not returned. Jennings would not go away quietly. Aided by a pair of 15-yard penalties against the Irish, SMU returned to the red zone. Notre Dame rallied for one final stand to keep the Mustangs out of the end zone. Four consecutive passes by Jennings yielded only three yards. The Irish again took over in the shadow of their own goal and proceeded to run out the clock. Jaden Greathouse suffered a wrist injury (Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire) Despite 312 passing yards by Carr and 152 more on the ground, it was hardly a satisfying performance. Turnovers and costly penalties have become more commonplace. Carr’s penchant for ignoring open receivers to make low percentage home run throws is somewhat concerning. A larger issue is the injuries that are piling up. Talich is likely lost for the season and Greathouse left the game with a wrist injury. His replacement, Mylan Graham, cannot seem to connect with Carr despite being open. Star linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa also departed early with an apparent injury. Let us review the answers to our pregame questions: Can SMU’s struggling offensive line give Jennings a chance to shine? Jennings was a mediocre 24 of 45 for 216 yards and one interception. He hit some big plays but was terrible in the red zone where Notre Dame turned up the pressure. Will Notre Dame exceed 200 yards rushing? No. SMU took away the run for the most part except for one long gain by James. He finished with 98 yards on 15 carries. Can the Irish secondary cover the Mustang receivers and tight ends? Coverage was shaky at times. Pressure on Jennings forced him to miss open receivers. Also, Irish cornerback Christian Gray had a rough night. Talich usually erases a number of mistakes on the back end. He spent most of the night on the sideline in a boot. Will Carr use play-action to set up explosive passing plays? I did not see much play-action. Mostly, CJ just chucked it downfield with mixed results. Can White and the SMU pass rushers get past the Irish offensive line? SMU earned one sack that was attributable to good coverage downfield. Otherwise, Carr had time to throw without pressure. Will Brewu, Jagusah, or Johnson make a splash upon their return? Brewu and Jason Onye had a few snaps and held up well. Jagusah got on the field to block for extra points and in victory formation. Johnson did not play, largely because Talich got hurt. It was not worth the risk to put Johnson out there. Can Notre Dame’s special teams make a meaningful contribution? Scaife’s 76-yard punt was memorable. The Irish responded well when SMU tried to advance the ball on a botched field goal attempt. Will a convincing win by the Irish drop them out of the playoffs? Notre Dame was never in danger but the Committee will almost certainly denigrate their performance. They are rapidly running out of mediocre teams to put ahead of the Irish, though. A few players stood out with excellent performances. Faison made up for an early fumble with seven receptions for 109 yards and an amazing touchdown. The pass blocking was excellent once again. Kudos to the linemen including Owen Strebig, who filled in for Will Black. On defense, Sanders played well as did Viliamu-Asa. Finally, Boubacar Traore was the star of the show for the Irish. NFL scouts are going to love his film from this game. It was a rough day for several teams. UCLA lost its first game and also their quarterback. Indiana fell to Washington and lost star receiver Nick Marsh and a starting offensive lineman. Ohio State has simply lost its way. Notre Dame avoided losing this game but the attrition on defense is alarming. Next week’s regular season finale at Syracuse should be an opportunity to rest key starters. Hopefully, the loyal Irish fan base will be able to relax as well. It has been a stressful second half of the season. The post Defense Carries Irish Over SMU appeared first on NDNation .

(Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Before the eleventh Sunday of the 2026 regular season kicks off, let’s have some fun by taking a look at the lines for the NFL Week 11 games. You can CLICK HERE for straight up NFL picks without regard to the spread. My overall record this season is 71-76-2, which is slightly ahead of the collective BGN community at 69-78-2. We’re slowly but surely trying to creep above .500. Here are suggestions when trying to beat the odds. NFL WEEK 11 GAMES NEW ORLEANS SAINTS at CHICAGO BEARS (-11.5): The Bears are coming off their bye. The Saints only have two losses this season by more than one possession … and those were back in early October. But Chicago’s offense is capable of scoring enough to cover this line. PICK: Bears -11.5 Loading… BALTIMORE RAVENS at CAROLINA PANTHERS (-2.5): The Panthers aren’t really worth believing in. The Ravens have enough fight in them to pick up a much-needed win in order to try to keep their season afloat. Jacoby Brissett has had more time to get comfortable with the offense. PICK: Ravens +2.5 Loading… MIAMI DOLPHINS at BUFFALO BILLS (-16.5): That’s … a lot of points! But am I really going to bet on Kyle McCord in his return to upstate New York over Josh Allen? No. PICK: Bills -16.5 Loading… TENNESSEE TITANS at DALLAS COWBOYS (-7.5): The Dallas defense is truly dreadful. That being said, I’m not so sure this Titans team has a pulse. Maybe going away from Christian Parker can actually help a little. Even if it won’t, the Cowboys should be able to score enough to cover. item.title: 'He will see what Man Utd are made of' - Pulis on Pochettino's first game
item.description: [BBC] Stepping into a job like Mauricio Pochettino has done at Manchester United, where managers have come and gone frequently, will always lead you to wonder why the others have not lasted very long. Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion. So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad. Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game. Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference. A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one. With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them. I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated. Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too. My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players. You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed. Pochettino had his first training session with United's players on Thursday [Getty Images] 'What your own eyes tell you is most important' I would have selected my team before I met the players, through my own knowledge and also with help from within. Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion. So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad. Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game. Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference. A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one. With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them. I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated. Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too. My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players. You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed. Pochettino had his first training session with United's players on Thursday [Getty Images] 'What your own eyes tell you is most important' I would have selected my team before I met the players, through my own knowledge and also with help from within. Whichever club I went in at, I'd expect to know something about most of the players within the group in terms of their position and ability, but understanding the character of the squad was vital too. The existing staff would know more about the lads' qualities in that respect than myself or anyone who had just arrived with me, so I'd always discuss that with the people I had inherited, from fitness coaches to the medical department. It's what your own eyes tell you that is most important, however. Going into your first game gives you the opportunity to see for yourself what your players are made of - and it can be a completely different view from what other people see. Most of the early games I managed would be hit and miss in terms of selection, but I would quickly work out the strengths and weaknesses of the group. As I've mentioned in previous columns, one of my first aims at any club where I was manager was about putting out a team, not a group of individuals. It does not take long to see when that is not happening. I can remember my first game of my first spell at Stoke, a 4-2 defeat at Walsall in the Championship. I wasn't universally enamoured by certain crowd favourites in that team and, while any manager knows that leaving some of them out could have an adverse effect on the supporters' view of yourself, you have to stand up and make decisions based on what you see. It is the same if there are other issues with the squad you have inherited too. West Brom's first game after I was appointed manager was a draw with West Ham on New Year's Day 2015. I sat in the stands at Upton Park with my son, Anthony, who was concerned how different the Albion team was compared to Crystal Palace, the last team I had managed in the Premier League. He was right to worry about it, but we still found a way - a totally different way of playing, but still a way to win that suited the group. Pulis (far right) watched West Brom play West Ham with (right to left) his son Anthony, his assistant Dave Kemp and the Baggies' technical director, Terry Burton [Getty Images] All your staff have to understand your objectives My initial aims after arriving at any club mid-season were pretty direct and also pretty basic too. The staff I inherited did not just know the players, they were also the first group who had to understand my objectives and also my principles - like the work ethic I expected, for example. Irrespective of what they were used to doing, it was imperative they followed my lead. One of the clubs I arrived at were struggling at the foot of the table and also suffering from a glut of injuries. In my opinion, the players were taking advantage of a very honest and hard-working medical department, who were quite accommodating on the treatment times for the lads. I changed that immediately, so injured players were treated at 9am, 2pm and 4pm, with sessions in-between those times for strength and recovery workouts. This did not go down well with the players because it impeded on their social lives and, in one case, a player whose injury record was not exactly brilliant came to me complaining that his wife expected him to pick his children up from school and being asked to be in at 4pm affected his private life too. I did not budge, and funnily enough the player in question recovered quite quickly - as did the majority of the other injured players. 'Clear the treatment rooms, and make sure the players are fit' Pulis at work on the training ground with West Brom in 2015 [Getty Images] Asking injured players to be at the training ground all day was by far the best way of getting them fit, in my experience, and the medical departments I managed were all working well past 4pm anyway so it was no hardship to them. Just on that side of things, I would sometimes get the feeling some medical departments thought that, if they weren't treating players, then they weren't doing their jobs. That was completely the opposite to how I saw it. I would congratulate people for having empty treatment rooms and applaud them for their work. Treatment rooms are comfort areas that certain players would always gravitate to, to have a kiss and a cuddle if they are feeling sorry for themselves for not being in the team. That's one of the first things that has to change, because you cannot give your players any excuses or hiding places if they are not performing. Similarly, I have always laughed at new managers who take over in mid-season and complain about the lack of fitness in their squad. I am sure I have done it myself at some point, but then I had a reputation of managing extremely fit squads of players and it was always an area I studied really closely. Early on in my management career, we weren't blessed with the advanced fitness equipment used in football today, but I was still able to quickly arrive at the level I believed the players should be at. How? Simple. Firstly, I had my own fitness runs that were tried and tested but, also, I knew that if during a fitness session they weren't moaning and sweating, they weren't working hard enough. Privately, you can realise very quickly when and which additions to the squad are needed. Pochettino will no doubt be thinking about that at United already, but he has 10 games in the Premier League and Champions League before the January transfer window opens. In the meantime, everything has to be geared towards winning games. I always knew I needed to do that quickly, because it helps the players believe in what I was doing, which is important too. I've outlined my principles I held at every club above, and they never changed, but my playing principles were determined by the quality of the group I inherited. M

item.title: Davis Schneider Issues Statement After Blue Jays Non-Tender Him
item.description: Davis Schneider Blue Jays Getty Former Toronto Blue Jays second baseman and outfielder Davis Schneider issued a statement after he was non-tendered by the team. The Blue Jays non-tendered Schneider on Friday, sending him to free agency immediately after parts of four seasons with the club. Now, he has spoken out following his release. Davis Schneider Grateful to Blue Jays Speaking to Canadian baseball writer Danny Gallagher, Schneider shared his first comments since the Blue Jays released him. “I was kind of expecting it. I knew it might happen. It’s part of the business. It’s part of the game. I’m not going to grind about it too much. It’s one of those things. Life goes on,” Schneider said. “I spent 9½ years with the organization. Toronto is one of the greatest cities I could play for, in the whole country, in all of North America. It’s such a great fan base that wants you to succeed. Toronto fans are the best in the world.” In an exclusive interview with non-tendered Davis Schneider, he told me: "I was kind of expecting it. I knew it might happen. It's part of the business. It's part of the game. I'm not going to grind about it too much. It's one of those things. Life goes on.'' — Danny Gallagher (@dannogallagher7) November 21, 2026 (2) More Davis Schneider: "I spent 9½ years with the organization. Toronto is one of the greatest cities I could play for, in the whole country, in all of North America. It's such a great fan base that wants you to succeed. Toronto fans are the best in the world.'' — Danny Gallagher (@dannogallagher7) November 21, 2026 Where Will Davis Schneider Play Next? The Blue Jays non-tendered Schneider because they did not want to pay his arbitration projection of $1.3 million next year. However, that doesn’t mean that his team in MLB is over, as another team could sign him for something less than that. Teams like the Los Angeles Angels and Colorado Rockies, who need an influx of talent at pretty much every position, should be the first ones to call up Schneider’s agent and see if he would be interested in signing with them, either on a cheap major-league deal, or on a minor-league deal with an invitation to spring training next season. Schneider has some pop in his bat, and he can play left field and second base, so he provides some versatility for whatever team he is on. He is also a great teammate and a fan favorite, so there are a lot of positives to signing him. It’s unfortunate that his time in Toronto ended, but with the Blue Jays looking to improve their roster after missing the playoffs, they had to make some tough decisions, and that meant not tendering Schneider a new contract. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Davis Schneider Issues Statement After Blue Jays Non-Tender Him appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 'Goosebumps!' - Super-sub Carlos Espi salutes Bernabeu roar after bailing out Real Madrid against Celta
item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Carlos Espi admitted the Santiago Bernabeu atmosphere gave him "goosebumps" after his 85th-minute rebound secured Real Madrid's 2-1 comeback win over Celta Vigo. The young striker stressed squad unity as Los Blancos extended their winning streak to nine matches ahead of Tuesday's Champions League battle. Espi completes late Bernabeu comeback Carlos Espi struck in the 85th minute to seal a 2-1 comeback victory for Real Madrid against Celta Vigo and extend their winning run to nine consecutive matches. After Pablo Duran gave Celta a sixth-minute lead and Kylian Mbappe blazed a first-half penalty over the crossbar, Jude Bellingham levelled on 66 minutes before Espi pounced on a rebound from Vinicius Junior's cross. The decisive finish marked the Valencian forward's fourth goal of the campaign and preserved Real Madrid's perfect home record this season. Speaking after the final whistle, Espi admitted the backing from the stands left a powerful impression on him. Match-winner reveals 'goosebumps' from crowd support Espi explained that every substitute entered the pitch determined to turn the contest around , crediting the collective spirit inside the 23-to-24-man squad alongside the vocal home crowd. "I get goosebumps," Espi said. "It's indescribable how much support I feel from everyone. I will give my all for the madridistas and for this club. I try to do what the coach asks of me, and every minute I get, I will make the most of it. If I can help the team, even better. As I said the other day, the goal is to stay united. We're 23-24 players, and we all need to move in the same direction. Those of us who came on did so fully focused on securing the victory, and that's what we achieved." Home fortress fuels ninth straight triumph While Real Madrid endured a frustrating opening half, Espi insisted dropping points at the Santiago Bernabeu was never an option once the crowd lifted the team in the second period. "Honestly, the fans are incredible; they support us from the very first minute," he added. "Today, they carried us forward. We can't afford to drop points here. Honestly, it's a real energy boost. It was a tough match that we managed to win, and now we have to keep moving forward because this doesn't stop—there's another battle in the Champions League." Full focus shifts to Tuesday's Champions League tie With only 48 hours to recover from a demanding domestic test, Espi stressed that Los Blancos must immediately channel their momentum into European action. "Now, the most important thing is Tuesday because this doesn't stop," he concluded. "We have two days to prepare for the match, and with all our enthusiasm, we're going for it."

item.title: Bucks’ Tyler Herro Makes NBA History Despite 13-Game Losing Streak
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks in action during a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks have spent much of November searching for a win. At least, Tyler Herro gave them a performance for the NBA record books. Herro scored a career-high 50 points against Philadelphia on Nov. 21. He added 11 rebounds and seven assists, carrying Milwaukee within one shot of overtime. The Bucks lost 132-129. But the team highlighted a piece of league history that belonged to its guard alone. In its announcement on X , Milwaukee called Herro the “first player in NBA history” to reach four statistical thresholds together. Tyler Herro is the first player in NBA history to have 50+ PTS, 11+ REB, 7+ 3PM, and 65% FG in a single game. pic.twitter.com/8PTq15qp53 — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 21, 2026 Bucks Announce Tyler Herro’s Historic Stat Line Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) The Bucks said Herro became the first player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 11 rebounds and seven made 3-pointers while shooting at least 65% from the field in a single game. That distinction covers all four marks together. It does not mean Herro became the first player to record 50 points and 11 rebounds. His efficiency made the scoring total stand out. The game’s box score lists him at 15-for-23 from the floor and 7-for-12 from beyond the arc. Those figures work out to 65.2% overall and 58.3% on 3-pointers. Herro made all 13 free throws, too. He needed only 23 field-goal attempts to reach 50 points, with his trips to the line providing more than a quarter of that total. He contributed in areas other than his shot-making. The guard grabbed three offensive rebounds and eight defensive boards, handed out seven assists and committed two turnovers in nearly 40 minutes. The outburst followed a rough stretch. The NBA’s game log shows Herro scored 18, five, eight and 19 points in his previous four appearances. He matched that combined total against the 76ers. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Milwaukee Bucks have spent much of November searching for a win. At least, Tyler Herro gave them a performance for the NBA record books. Herro scored a career-high 50 points against Philadelphia on Nov. 21. He added 11 rebounds and seven assists, carrying Milwaukee within one shot of overtime. The Bucks lost 132-129. But the team highlighted a piece of league history that belonged to its guard alone. In its announcement on X , Milwaukee called Herro the “first player in NBA history” to reach four statistical thresholds together. Tyler Herro is the first player in NBA history to have 50+ PTS, 11+ REB, 7+ 3PM, and 65% FG in a single game. pic.twitter.com/8PTq15qp53 — Milwaukee Bucks (@Bucks) November 21, 2026 Bucks Announce Tyler Herro’s Historic Stat Line Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 21: Tyler Herro #11 of the Milwaukee Bucks drives against Dominick Barlow #25 of the Philadelphia 76ers during the first half of a game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 21, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) The Bucks said Herro became the first player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 11 rebounds and seven made 3-pointers while shooting at least 65% from the field in a single game. That distinction covers all four marks together. It does not mean Herro became the first player to record 50 points and 11 rebounds. His efficiency made the scoring total stand out. The game’s box score lists him at 15-for-23 from the floor and 7-for-12 from beyond the arc. Those figures work out to 65.2% overall and 58.3% on 3-pointers. Herro made all 13 free throws, too. He needed only 23 field-goal attempts to reach 50 points, with his trips to the line providing more than a quarter of that total. He contributed in areas other than his shot-making. The guard grabbed three offensive rebounds and eight defensive boards, handed out seven assists and committed two turnovers in nearly 40 minutes. The outburst followed a rough stretch. The NBA’s game log shows Herro scored 18, five, eight and 19 points in his previous four appearances. He matched that combined total against the 76ers. Herro’s Final Shot Arrives Too Late for Bucks Milwaukee nearly turned the milestone into a comeback win. As Field Level Media reported via Reuters , Philadelphia led by 10 with just over two minutes remaining. Herro helped cut the deficit before Brayden Burries hit a 3-pointer with 4.8 seconds left. Two Philadelphia free throws left Milwaukee trailing by three. With 1.5 seconds remaining, the Bucks found Herro on the inbound pass. His shot went in, but replay showed the ball remained on his fingertips when time expired. The reversal left him at 50 points and sent Milwaukee home with another loss. The result dropped the Bucks to 1-16 and extended their losing streak to 13 games, according to the Associated Press game report . The shooting for Herro marked a sharp difference from his recent outings. He went a combined 0-for-10 from deep against Atlanta and Miami, then made four of seven against Portland. He carried that improved touch into Philadelphia. Milwaukee needs that production to last for many afternoons. Herro supplied points, rebounds and passing against the 76ers, and the team still finished one possession short. His final basket could have bought five more minutes. Instead, the Bucks left with a record-setting performance and the same losing streak. item.title: 14-year-old Adrian Peterson Jr. receives offer from Oklahoma
item.description: BRYAN TERRY/THE OKLAHOMAN / USA TODAY NETWORK 14-year-old Adrian Peterson Jr. receives offer from Oklahoma appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Oklahoma has extended a scholarship offer to Adrian Peterson Jr., giving the son of former Sooners standout and NFL running back Adrian Peterson an opportunity to follow in his father’s footsteps in Norman. The 14-year-old announced Saturday on social media that he received an offer from the Sooners. A member of the 2030 recruiting class, Peterson Jr. is currently a freshman at Fort Bend Ridge Point High School in Missouri City, Texas. He is listed at 6-foot-1 and 175 pounds and has experience playing multiple positions, including running back, wide receiver and defensive back. Peterson Jr. has already attracted considerable attention from college programs. His scholarship offers include Miami, Florida State, Texas Tech, Texas A&M, Baylor, Minnesota, Syracuse, TCU, SMU, UTSA, Missouri State and Texas State, along with Oklahoma, according to 247Sports. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The young athlete has begun making an impact at the high school level. Through six games, he has recorded seven receptions for 95 yards and two touchdowns, according to MaxPreps. His father became one of the Sooners’ most accomplished players between 2004 and 2006. Adrian Peterson Sr. racked up 4,041 rushing yards and 41 touchdowns across three seasons with the Sooners, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. He was a unanimous All-American in 2004, finished as the Heisman Trophy runner-up and earned first-team All-Big 12 recognition in each of his three seasons. Peterson Sr. eventually carried that success into the NFL, finishing his 15-year professional career with 14,918 rushing yards, the fifth-highest total among running backs in league history. With Oklahoma now among the programs pursuing his son, the Sooners have an opportunity to add another member of the Peterson family to their football program when the 2030 recruiting cycle arrives. He was a unanimous All-American in 2004, finished as the Heisman Trophy runner-up and earned first-team All-Big 12 recognition in each of his three seasons. Peterson Sr. eventually carried that success into the NFL, finishing his 15-year professional career with 14,918 rushing yards, the fifth-highest total among running backs in league history. With Oklahoma now among the programs pursuing his son, the Sooners have an opportunity to add another member of the Peterson family to their football program when the 2030 recruiting cycle arrives. item.title: Maple Leafs Need to Fire Jim Hiller After Latest Collapse
item.description: Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty The time has come for the Toronto Maple Leafs to grow some stones and fire head coach Jim Hiller. This statement isn’t some knee-jerk reaction to the team’s most recent loss. It’s a natural consequence of yet another third-period collapse. The Maple Leafs were leading 3-1 midway through the second period before three unanswered goals led to a Columbus Blue Jackets’ 4-3 win. But it was the two goals roughly a minute apart that added insult to injury. Sure, Hiller wasn’t on the ice for the two goals. He wasn’t playing in goal. He wasn’t the guy who didn’t block a shot or clear the puck from the zone. However, someone has to be accountable for the situation. Someone has to answer to the latest debacle. And as much as the players are to blame for the situation, the bottom line is that the ax has to fall somewhere, and that somewhere will be Jim Hiller’s head. Do the Maple Leafs Have Any Other Choice? While it’s easy to call for the coach’s head, the fact of the matter is: Do the Maple Leafs have any other choice? Does the organization have any other realistic path forward? Hiller doesn’t seem to have an answer for any of what’s going on. He doesn’t seem to grasp the seriousness of the situation befalling the team. Meanwhile, GM John Chayka is feeling the heat. He’s the guy responsible for hiring Hiller. That’s why one has to think that there is no other way around this. Chayka can either fess up to his mistake and try to right the wrong, or stubbornly try to wiggle his way out of the mess. It’s clear that he’s out of runway. The Maple Leafs are in a death spiral with no clear end in sight. Something has to give. Unless there’s a magic solution that no one is aware of, the Leafs don’t really have any other choice. The chain will have to break in the weakest link, and that link is Jim Hiller. Any Option Is Better Than Nothing at This Point Yes, it’s true that no move is better than a bad move. That situation applied to the Leafs a week ago. Now, that’s not the case anymore. While the goal is not to make a gut-call at this time, the fact is that something will have to change. The Maple Leafs cannot afford to let this latest mess go unanswered. It will either have to be a massive trade to really shake the team up, or it will have to be a coaching change. The latter is the easiest way out for now. It’s also worth noting that a coaching change won’t preclude a trade. Nevertheless, Chayka can’t tip his hand right now. Everyone knows he’s in a bind. So, there won’t be any compassion from any other GM out there. Let’s see what happens. The Maple Leafs next game will be on Monday night in Long Island against the Islanders. That gives the organization very little time to make a decision, if any. Regardless of the tight turnaround, there may be no other way out. item.title: Yahoo Top 10: Wild Week 12 shakes up college football rankings
item.description: The most mundane weekends in college football can often turn into mayhem. Two of the Big Ten's best playoff challengers (UCLA and Indiana) lost, preseason No. 1 Ohio State took a fourth 'L' this season and LSU — its high-priced head coach, Lane Kiffin, and $40 million-plus roster — dropped a fifth game. The Bruins and Hoosiers served up the biggest surprises with overtime losses at Michigan and Washington, respectively, tossing the conference into a bit of chaos and uncertainty. Can the Big Ten win a fourth straight national championship ? At this point, the odds seem steep for even getting more than two teams into the playoff. Also in the conference, Ohio State became the first preseason top-ranked team to lose at least four games since USC in 2012 as the Buckeyes dropped a game at Nebraska. In the SEC, Tennessee kept its playoff hopes alive with a throttling of LSU in Knoxville, and Georgia survived the always-scary trip to Columbia, South Carolina. The Big 12 race is Utah, BYU and Texas Tech. Meanwhile, Miami and Wake Forest are on a collision course for a rematch in Charlotte (the Hurricanes won Round 1, 33-20) for all the ACC marbles. 1. Utah Utes This week: beat TCU 38-17 Next week: vs. West Virginia The Utes blew open a 17-17 tie with three consecutive touchdowns in the final six minutes of the game. QB Devon Dampier scored the last two TDs — one passing and another rushing — on a night when he led the team on the ground and through the air. Dampier had more than 325 total yards and Larry Simmons caught three passes for a whopping 114 yards as Utah clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance. 2. Georgia Bulldogs This week: beat South Carolina 34-6 Next week: vs. Georgia Tech Is anyone playing better football than Kirby Smart’s crew? Smart's team turned a tight game into a blowout in the second half, even recovering a surprise onside kick in the third quarter. Gunner Stockton continues to be one of the nation's leaders in efficiency (19 of 23) and the Bulldogs know how to run the ball (Nate Frazier had 94 yards). But DC Glenn Schumann's defensive unit was great from the start in Columbia on Saturday night. Ethan Barbour and the Georgia Bulldogs have plenty of reasons to flex these days. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish This week: beat SMU 24-3 Next week: at Syracuse After beating Miami and bludgeoning SMU, there is little argument that the Irish, with a season-ending win over Syracuse next week, will make the 12-team postseason. The loss to BYU stings, sure, but Notre Dame QB CJ Carr continues to be one of the biggest challengers in the Heisman Trophy race. He threw for more than 300 yards against the Mustangs. 4. Miami Hurricanes This week: beat Virginia Tech 28-20 Next week: vs. Boston College Down 14-0? No problem. The Hurricanes mounted a comeback at Hard Rock Stadium to solidify a trip to Charlotte for the ACC championship game — despite QB Darian Mensah not throwing a single touchdown pass. In fact, he

item.content:encoded: The most mundane weekends in college football can often turn into mayhem. Two of the Big Ten's best playoff challengers (UCLA and Indiana) lost, preseason No. 1 Ohio State took a fourth 'L' this season and LSU — its high-priced head coach, Lane Kiffin, and $40 million-plus roster — dropped a fifth game. The Bruins and Hoosiers served up the biggest surprises with overtime losses at Michigan and Washington, respectively, tossing the conference into a bit of chaos and uncertainty. Can the Big Ten win a fourth straight national championship ? At this point, the odds seem steep for even getting more than two teams into the playoff. Also in the conference, Ohio State became the first preseason top-ranked team to lose at least four games since USC in 2012 as the Buckeyes dropped a game at Nebraska. In the SEC, Tennessee kept its playoff hopes alive with a throttling of LSU in Knoxville, and Georgia survived the always-scary trip to Columbia, South Carolina. The Big 12 race is Utah, BYU and Texas Tech. Meanwhile, Miami and Wake Forest are on a collision course for a rematch in Charlotte (the Hurricanes won Round 1, 33-20) for all the ACC marbles. 1. Utah Utes This week: beat TCU 38-17 Next week: vs. West Virginia The Utes blew open a 17-17 tie with three consecutive touchdowns in the final six minutes of the game. QB Devon Dampier scored the last two TDs — one passing and another rushing — on a night when he led the team on the ground and through the air. Dampier had more than 325 total yards and Larry Simmons caught three passes for a whopping 114 yards as Utah clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance. 2. Georgia Bulldogs This week: beat South Carolina 34-6 Next week: vs. Georgia Tech Is anyone playing better football than Kirby Smart’s crew? Smart's team turned a tight game into a blowout in the second half, even recovering a surprise onside kick in the third quarter. Gunner Stockton continues to be one of the nation's leaders in efficiency (19 of 23) and the Bulldogs know how to run the ball (Nate Frazier had 94 yards). But DC Glenn Schumann's defensive unit was great from the start in Columbia on Saturday night. Ethan Barbour and the Georgia Bulldogs have plenty of reasons to flex these days. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images 3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish This week: beat SMU 24-3 Next week: at Syracuse After beating Miami and bludgeoning SMU, there is little argument that the Irish, with a season-ending win over Syracuse next week, will make the 12-team postseason. The loss to BYU stings, sure, but Notre Dame QB CJ Carr continues to be one of the biggest challengers in the Heisman Trophy race. He threw for more than 300 yards against the Mustangs. 4. Miami Hurricanes This week: beat Virginia Tech 28-20 Next week: vs. Boston College Down 14-0? No problem. The Hurricanes mounted a comeback at Hard Rock Stadium to solidify a trip to Charlotte for the ACC championship game — despite QB Darian Mensah not throwing a single touchdown pass. In fact, he had two interceptions to match his season total to this point. But Miami's defense rose to the challenge after the early hole, forcing Tech into five punts on its next seven drives. 5. Wake Forest Demon Deacons This week: beat Georgia Tech 50-29 Next week: vs. Duke If there was still any doubt that the Demon Deacons are real playoff challengers, those should be put to bed. Jake Dickert's team has outscored its last seven opponents 363-67. QB Gio Lopez threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more in the shellacking of the Yellow Jackets. Wake is barreling toward an ACC championship game appearance and a playoff spot. 6. Alabama Crimson Tide This week: beat Chattanooga 47-0 Next week: vs. Auburn The Tide rested Keelon Russell, and why not? The 7-5 FCS Mocs didn't stand a chance. Seven of Chattanooga's 10 drives lasted three plays or less. Kane Wommack, a candidate for several head coaching gigs, and his defensive unit has allowed 20 points the last three games. Bama is headed to the playoff with a win in the Iron Bowl. 7. UCLA Bruins This week: lost to Michigan 18-16 (3OT) Next week: vs. USC Michigan QB Bryce Underwood completed just 11 passes and was sacked four times. And while that doesn't sound like the stat line of a winner, the Bruins offense couldn't muster enough to beat the Wolverines. Ty Dieffenbach was sacked four times, threw an interception and lost a costly fumble that set up Michigan for the go-ahead score. 8. Texas Longhorns This week: beat Arkansas 45-3 Next week: vs. Texas A&M Arch Manning had four incompletions and three touchdowns in the win over the lowly Razorbacks. There's no hiding the Longhorns' deficiencies, but Texas has the talent to win it all and a victory over the Aggies next week will send them to the 12-team playoff. After back-to-back losses to Florida and Oklahoma, the Horns have won five straight. 9. Iowa Hawkeyes This week: beat Illinois 34-17 Next week: vs. Nebraska No one benefitted from Saturday's Big Ten upset bonanza quite like the Hawkeyes. They are now in striking distance to advance to the playoff. And who would want to play Phil Parker's defense and an offensive unit that moves the ball better than any Hawkeye version in years. Iowa shut out the Illini in the second half and backup RB L.J. Phillips, in for the injured Kamari Moulton, ran for 154 yards — this third straight 100-yard outing. 10. Tennessee Volunteers This week: beat LSU 27-13 Next week: at Vanderbilt When in doubt, run QB Faizon Brandon. That's what the Vols did. He ran for 112 yards on just 12 carries — nearly 10 yards a pop — and scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter. It was more than enough for Tennessee to re-enter our Top 10 ahead of a big game in Nashville next week. Win and they're (likely) in the postseason.

item.title: No. 17 Boise State suffers costly loss to San Diego State after late clock-management snafu
item.description: San Diego State defenders celebrate after recovering a fumble by Boise State quarterback Maddux Madsen on Saturday in Boise, Idaho. AP Photo/Darin Oswald San Diego State hit a field goal as time expired to beat No. 17 Boise State 22-20 in a stunning upset Saturday night on Boise's famed blue turf. Cooper DiLeva's winning 42-yard kick deals a serious blow to Boise's College Football Playoff hopes, which it could earn by finishing the season as the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Broncos (9-2) are by no means out of playoff contention, and will still play for the Pac-12 title in two weeks, but the loss opens the door for another G6 contender. BALL. GAME. San Diego State will be back at Boise in two weeks to compete for a Pac-12 Championship 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LE2aLr97sy — USA Sports (@usasports) November 22, 2026 SDSU's victory was made possible by a bizarre sequence in the final minutes as the Broncos were trying to run out the clock with the ball. On third-and-8 with 1:41 on the clock, BSU threw a pass that ended up with tight end Keawe Browne out of bounds, which stopped the clock at 1:36. The Aztecs had zero timeouts so that was a huge favor. On the next play, fourth-and-3 at the SDSU 45-yard line, BSU tried for the first down rather than punting and pinning back the Aztecs. Quarterback Maddux Madsen was stuffed for a loss, giving SDSU the ball in prime field position with 1:31 left on the clock. The Aztecs (6-5) quickly drove into field-goal range to set up the winning kick. SDSU QB Stone Saunders played a part in both of his team's touchdowns, scoring on a 9-yard run in the third quarter and throwing a 39-yard scoring pass to Jaylon Hawkins with 1:58 to play. San Diego could have tied it with a PAT at that point but opted to go for 2 and came up short. That gave Boise State the ball with a 20-19 lead and under two minutes to play, but the Broncos weren't able to close out the victory.

item.title: WSL roundup: Chelsea thwarted by Liverpool keeper, London City move to third
item.description: Keating’s resilience keeps Chelsea at bay in 0-0 draw Van de Donk and Putellas score twice to sink Palace 6-2 Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea , the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point, while London City Lionesses moved to within four points of the top by beating Crystal Palace 6-2. After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night , Chelsea drew a blank. Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after they beat City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short. Continue reading...

item.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation. Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager. Continue reading...

item.title: Raya injured but Madueke rescues point for Arsenal in seesaw Newcastle draw
item.description: If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park. Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team and he certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside, where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back commendably to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance. At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and subtle tactical rejig suggested he is no mug after all. item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

item.description: Boro beat Bristol City 2-0; Stoke 1-0 Birmingham Scott Parker still winless as West Ham held by Preston Middlesbrough scored a goal either side of half-time to climb to the top of the Championship with a 2-0 win that piled further pressure on the Bristol City manager Michael Skubala. Adilson Malanda’s header five minutes before half-time was followed by David Strelec’s finish in the 54th minute to secure victory. The three points were effectively secured before Middlesbrough head coach Kim Hellberg introduced the division’s top scorer, Will Lankshear, for the final 14 minutes from the bench after injury. item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

Brady and Spiro, who is representing the planned Fifa investor Joshua Kushner in a legal battle against Uefa, would become limited partners in Clearlake with no voting rights at Chelsea if the transactions are completed. item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Continue reading...

item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. Continue reading...

Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational
item.description: The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history. Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville. Continue reading...

He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds. Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons. item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards.
